title: European Commission confirms AI-generated cyberattack that took HR and other applications offline
date_note: Date of the report; Politico, relayed by Izvestia, says the attack had been going on for more than 10 days.
summary: Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed an AI-generated cyber campaign, detected 22 October, misusing a publicly available AI tool he did not name. Several applications were taken down, most since restored; Politico (via SecurityWeek) named Sysper and MyPMO. He said no data breach affecting staff as a whole was detected. Gazeta.ru, citing Reuters, reports Regnier said the EU Academy platform, which stopped working on 23 November, was affected and that its users' personal data leaked.
plain: The European Commission confirmed an AI-generated cyber campaign against it. It took several applications offline as a precaution and most are back. It has found no evidence of a data breach affecting staff as a whole.
exec: An AI-generated campaign hit an EU institution; the Commission says it has detected no evidence of a data breach affecting staff as a whole.
action: If you work with EU institutions, expect notices from them and treat unexpected messages claiming to be from Commission staff with care.
impact: Several applications taken down as a protective measure, most since restored (Regnier); Sysper and MyPMO reported offline, restored early in the week of 16 Nov (heise); most staff received salaries as usual but some could not file time sheets or arrange leave (Politico, via Izvestia, citing two officials); no evidence of a data breach affecting staff as a whole detected, investigation ongoing (Regnier); per SecurityWeek, Regnier said he was not aware of a ransom demand and did not attribute the attack to a known group; per Politico, CERT-EU linked the tool ARTEX; Gazeta.ru, citing Reuters, reports Regnier said on 23 November the EU Academy platform was hit by the attack, leading to a leak of its users' personal data, with the investigation ongoing.

sources.name: The Telegraph via Yahoo News (relaying Politico)
Help Net Security (relaying the Commission briefing and Politico)

validation.note: Euronews (own anonymous official; Sysper and JSIS named) and Politico (relayed by Izvestia, Telegraph, Anadolu, La Libre) report independently; the Commission has not confirmed the scope. Politico original not read. 20 Nov: Security Affairs (19 Nov) reports CERT-EU named ARTEX as a possible tool and more than ten days of disruption; CERT-EU and Politico originals not read. 20 Nov: Help Net Security reports spokesperson Regnier confirming an AI-generated campaign at the Commission midday briefing; ARTEX link is Politico, not Commission; originals not read. 23 Nov: Gazeta.ru (23 Nov) relays Reuters quoting Regnier that the EU Academy platform was affected and users' personal data leaked; only Gazeta.ru read, Reuters original not read, academy.europa.eu answered 403, no second publisher found yet.

review.note: Compared with Help Net Security, SecurityWeek, Izvestia: Regnier AI-generated quote, 22 Oct detection, no breach evidence for staff as a whole, no ransom, no attribution match.
